subject: Renewal: Priority Support Stack & Phased Throughput/Latency SLA Addendum
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cloudcare.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@cloudcare.com
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion + request for priority support ladder and higher throughput SLA

Mina —

Thanks for the heads-up about the renewal window. We're preparing our FY27 budget and are evaluating a bump to the support level for our patient-facing inference tier. Two asks from my side:

1) Priority support (faster incident response + a named POC) for production-facing traffic starting at renewal.
2) A phased SLA that increases throughput/latency commitments over the next 6 months as we onboard new pipelines (we expect ~2.5x request growth).

I've attached a short doc with our expected traffic ramp and a list of questions from procurement. Can you confirm whether Redwood can offer a staged SLA addendum (with credits for missed p95/p99 latency targets during the ramp) and what the pricing delta would be?

Jordan
Director of Platform Engineering
CloudCare Health Systems

Attachment: 2026-04-14-cloudcare-request.pdf (1 page; traffic ramp + procurement questions)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cloudcare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + request for priority support ladder and higher throughput SLA

Jordan —

Appreciate the details and the traffic profile. Short answer: yes, we can support a staged SLA with an initial ramp window and a predictable upgrade path to a higher-throughput SLA. Proposed high-level approach below:

- Phase 1 (months 0–2 post-renewal): Named POC + Priority Support (1 hour initial response for high-severity incidents), monitored burst capacity to absorb first-stage growth.
- Phase 2 (months 2–4): Commitment to improved latency SLOs for the primary inference route (p95 target moves from 220ms -> 170ms), parallelization and dedicated reserved capacity increase triggered at 120% of baseline.
- Phase 3 (months 4–6): Full throughput SLA (sustained requests/minute) and tightened p99 targets with a rolling latency budget and credits if missed during steady-state.

We typically offer a ramp credit schedule where credit percentages scale down as you enter later phases. I'll need to firm up numbers with Ben (infra capacity & pricing). Can you confirm the following so we can draft an addendum?

- Exact traffic baseline (requests/min) today and expected at month 6;
- Any hard blackout windows or compliance gating for capacity changes;
- Preferred billing model for the uplift (monthly vs. annualized).

I'll attach a sample SLA phasing spreadsheet and a draft addendum once we align internally. If helpful, happy to set a 30-minute tech+commercial call later this week.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: sla-phasing-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet with proposed latency/credit bands)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@cloudcare.com>
Cc:
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + request for priority support ladder and higher throughput SLA

Mina / Jordan —

I reviewed the spike profile in your attachment. Technical notes / constraints:

- We can provision an initial reserved pool and a staged autoscale trigger at ~1.3x baseline quickly. That covers Phase 1 and the first half of Phase 2.
- To guarantee the later Phase 3 throughput SLOs we'll need a firm commit on committed reserved capacity (monthly commit) or a short-term burst budget with explicit overage caps.
- For latency improvements (p95 -> 170ms), we recommend enabling our KV prefix caching for the primary route and a 8-bit quantization profile for the 2nd-stage model variant; both are low-risk but require a brief QA window (3–5 business days).

Operational asks from CloudCare to hit phase timelines reliably:
- Access to a representative prompt/test set for pre-cutover QA;
- A weekly sync for the first 8 weeks during ramp;
- Agreement to commit to an initial reserved GPU capacity for months 3–6 if usage trends exceed 120% of baseline.

If you agree to the above, I'll draft an internal runbook and we can bake the runbook as an exhibit to the addendum.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Dedicated Ops | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + request for priority support ladder and higher throughput SLA

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the clear ask and for confirming the internal constraints. I've sketched commercial terms that map to Mina/Ben's technical approach:

- Pricing: 22% list uplift for Priority Support + phased reserved capacity commits (month-by-month ramp credits applied per SLA spreadsheet).
- Credits: 5% monthly credit if Phase 2 p95 target missed, then tumbling 3%/2% for later misses as phases progress (detailed in attached PDF).
- Term/Commit: 12-month renewal with an optional 6-month pilot clause allowing CloudCare to accelerate Phase 2 earlier if we meet agreed load test gates.

Next steps:
1) Jordan, please confirm baseline RPS and whether CloudCare prefers monthly billing for the uplift.
2) Contracts (cc'd) — we will prepare a short addendum (attached) reflecting the phased SLO exhibits and the runbook Ben will produce; seeking signature via DocuSign.

I'll include the draft addendum in DocuSign this afternoon. If that timeline doesn't work for procurement, ping me and we'll extend the signature window.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-draft-addendum-2026-04-21.pdf
